name: GAMUT
description: Rubric-based evaluation of open-ended generation faces a fundamental tension between expressiveness and reliability. Authoring a faithful rubric requires expressing the structure of the space of good answers: open-ended sets of acceptable options, ordered processes, and the relative importance of facts. Grading with the rubric requires a judge to score consistently, and judges are far more reliable on flat, binary checks than on rich structure. We resolve this tension with a two-level meta-rubric framework.
